questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was already at exchange here when I decided to extend my stay (required new application). Genevas international scene, potential career opportunities and course selection within public international law made me choose to stay another semester at UNIGE.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Campus is like KU, different faculties throughout town. It is not possible to live on campus, as far as I am concerned. 
It is generally difficult to find housing in Geneva, as the demand is high. I was lucky to get student residence. I managed to extend it, when I found out that I was approved for another semester, I contacted the residence. As soon as I applied for extension of my stay, I e-mailed them to ask about my possibilities of staying.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived just across the street from the faculty. However, do you get student housing, regardless of where it is in town, I would take it. Ghoising and living expenses in Geneva are high. Student housing is more favorable price wise.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The first week or so of classes, it is possible to try all the different classes that you might be interested in. I found this very nice, as it gives an opportunity to try the classes before choosing them. I didn’t buy the books/polycopié before after choosing. However, it was still possible to look through some of the material, as it is shared on Moodle too (corresponding to Absalon).  The course registration process is a two-step process, first you register for the courses. Later, you register for the exams. Everything is done through the university’s ‘portail’. It is very important that the courses you want to take and do the exam in, is registered twice (both the course registration and later the exam registration as well). As mentioned, you will be well informed about this multiple times.  If you are doing the CTL, courses need to be registered for the CTL. Things are explained when starting (introduction meeting). OBS you should apply for the CTL separately. This can be done before leaving for Geneva.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The student coordinated. The administration. Professor can guide to a certain extend, but will normally refer you to the secretary. 

The process of registering for courses at University de Genève is explained during the mandatory orientation meeting, in the flyer with the step-by-step overview and during the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
It is my understanding that you can register with all the classes within the Faculty of Law. However, there are some ‘seminars’ where UNIGE students have priority as these are mandatory for their memoire (master dissertation).

It is possible to take courses at different faculties - and institutes (as a part of the CTL). I took all my classes at the Faculty of Law as to why I have no experience with this. It was, however, once again well explained by Université de Genève.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to register for the courses and exams respectively. If courses and exams are taken as a part of the CTL, they should be registered specifically for this. It is explained once you get to the university.   Be aware, the CTL must be applied for separately. This can be done even before you arrive in Geneva.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I very much appreciated the selection within international law. The professors had a lot of relevant practical experience, usually from one of the international organizations located in Geneva. 

The expectations for the exam and the type of exam was, however, not very clear. I recommend that you ask the professor in the beginning of the course. I had different experiences where it was not clear to me what was expected, before being at the exam, where it was explained.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive to buy groceries and to eat and drink out. In general, Geneva is a quite expensive city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of active associations and sport and cultural opportunities through the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of different sports and cultural activities offered through the university. The student associations are very active and happy to welcome you.
Some of them are free. Others are offered at student friendly prices.
You can read more about it here:
https://vie-de-campus.unige.ch/sport-culture/sport
and here
https://www.unige.ch/dife/culture/

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I volunteered at the Croix-Rouge genevoise with an elderly lady two hours a week as well as at retirement home once a month. I had a lovely time. It was furthermore a really good way of getting insight in the Swiss culture, meeting locals and improving my French.
You can read more about it here:
https://www.croix-rouge-ge.ch/nos-activites
Even though my level of French was not very good and I couldn’t commit to the commitment period stated, they allowed me to start. As I was ensured through Croix-Rouge when I took part in the activities, I did not need a separate insurance.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
It is easy to get around Switzerland by train. Personally, I was interested in experiencing the four different languages spoken and how the culture differed in the different regions. I travelled with an interrail ticket, but you can also get some ‘supersaver tickets’ for a decent price. The nature is wonderful. I really enjoyed hiking.
You can check out this website and sign up for the newsletter to get recommendations on what to do in Geneva:
https://www.geneve.ch
I participated in the ESN introweek. It was a nice way to meet other exchange students. They also give you a good introduciton to the city, university etc.
If yo uare under 25 years old you can buy a ticket (around 100 CHF per year) and you can take all public transportation for free after 19:00. Weekends should apply.
Also, you can by a transportation pass (half-fare pass) where you get at 50% discount on tickets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust. Geneva is a wealthy and safe city. In many ways it reminds me of Copenhagen in that regard. Stores and restaurants close quite early and a lot of places are closed on Sundays. Applications etc. are mostly made by physical mail/post, not online.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I joined Croix-Rouge and talked to students in the different classes that I had. Do not be scared to initiate the conversation. Join a team sport or the musical. Generally, swiss people to keep to themselves. However, doing my classes in French, I met multiple swiss students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is safe and people are very polite. The society is organized and there is a high level of trust.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Université de Genève is a very good university both academically and regarding its activities (cultural and sports as well as student associations). 

Make use of free French classes. The sooner you sign up for the language classes, the greater chance there is to get your preferred class. 

Remember to explore Switzerland while you are there. It is an interesting country as the culture varies from the different parts of Switzerland.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are informed about the type of exam and the expectations.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I found my direction for my future career. 
I am very pleased that I managed to improve my French. 
I am very pleased with my personal relations and the network I have managed to get.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had to compromise my lifestyle due to the higher living expenses. However, I fouled alternatives which I was pleased with.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
